notes:
Klipr 2.15 — AI Review actually works, and a rebuilt Clips tab

**Run AI Review was broken, and it was hiding it**

Groq retired the model Klipr was asking for. The API answered with an error,
the code read a field that wasn't there, and the resulting crash was caught and
turned into an empty result — so the button ran, scored nothing, and looked
like it had worked. It has been dead since that model was dropped.

- Klipr now tries each of the models it knows about in turn, so the next
  retirement degrades instead of breaking.
- Failures say what the API actually reported, in red, instead of silently
  doing nothing.
- The button now shows "Scoring...", then how many clips it scored.

**AI Review now covers every clip**

- It used to score only clips already in the upload queue. Finished clips that
  had never been queued were skipped entirely. Now everything on the page can
  be scored.
- **Select a clip and press the button to score just that one.** With nothing
  selected it scores everything that has no score yet.
- Scores for clips that aren't queued are stored alongside their notes and
  tags, so scoring a clip no longer means putting it in line to be published.
- Large libraries are scored in batches. In one request the reply would come
  back truncated and nothing would be scored — the same silent failure as
  above.

**The AI Review tab is now about the AI**

- Scored, not yet scored, average score and best so far, across your clips.
- Each row leads with its score, coloured by how good it is, with the AI's own
  reasoning underneath instead of numbers you can already see.
- Filter to unscored clips only, and sort by best or worst score.
- Upload Schedule is collapsed into a single strip — it is set-once
  scheduling, not review, and it was taking the top third of the page. Click
  it to open.

**Clips is now a card grid**

- Every clip is a card: preview image, length, favourite star, Final or Raw,
  and a YouTube badge once queued. Title, streamer and age underneath.
- Search has a real Ctrl+K shortcut, and a Sort by control — newest, oldest,
  largest or by name.
- Selecting a clip brings up a row of actions across the top — Preview, Edit
  Clip, Change Headline, Rename, Publish to YouTube, Cancel Queue, Delete.
- The side panel is now Clip Details: a large preview you can click to play,
  the title, who it came from and when, and status, length, date and file size.
- The old list is still there — the toggle beside Sort by switches between
  them, and the grid reflows to however wide your window is.

**Fixes**

- **The preview in the side panel was a smear.** A Tk label measures itself in
  characters while it holds text but in pixels once it holds an image, so the
  placeholder's size was cropping every thumbnail to a sliver.
- **Pages scrolled when there was nothing to scroll.** Cards in the details
  column were locked to a fixed height whatever they held, leaving a large
  empty gap and hundreds of pixels of scroll into nothing. Cards now measure
  to their contents, and the mouse wheel does nothing when everything already
  fits — everywhere in Klipr.
- **A blank Clips page on a fresh install** now says "No clips yet" instead of
  showing an empty panel.
- **Clips no longer wait for memory that was already spent.** Before
  transcribing, Klipr checks there is room in RAM so that running low slows it
  down instead of killing the bot. That check asked for 1200 MB every time —
  the cost of loading Whisper from scratch — even when the model was already
  loaded, which it is for the whole of any busy session. It now asks for
  400 MB in that case, and stops waiting when free memory is not recovering,
  since that usually means the load is Klipr's own clip rendering.
